analysis.title: USA: ISM Manufacturing Above Expectations; September Construction Spending Well Below Expectations
key_insights: ISM manufacturing rose 1.0pt to 55.5 in October, above the GS and median forecast of 54.5. GS calls the composition mixed-to-strong.
New orders rose 0.2pt to 55.5 and production rose 2.3pt to 59.0, while employment edged down 0.3pt to 52.4.
Machinery respondents described business conditions as strong, citing the AI buildout and defense-related spending.
ISM prices paid fell 2.7pt to 75.2 after a large September increase. Respondents still cited inflationary pressure, volatile commodity markets and material shortages.

Supplier deliveries rose 0.1pt to 59.1, meaning slower deliveries for a larger share of respondents. Average lead time for production materials rose to 87 days, against a 2019 average of 67 days and a July 2022 peak of 100 days.

The S&P Global US manufacturing PMI was revised down 1.1pt to 54.9 in the October final reading, after September's level, the highest since May 2022. Output, new orders, employment, input prices and output prices were all revised down.
GS reads the ISM and PMI reports together as confirming a healthy pace of activity but no sign of a surge to a far above-trend pace.
Nominal construction spending fell 1.9% m/m in September, well below GS at +0.2% and the median at +0.3%, from an August level revised up 1.1pp to +2.0%.
The construction decline was almost entirely a 13% drop in private residential improvements, the largest in the series' history. The component has averaged a 6% m/m move over the past six months.
Private single family spending was flat, multi-family rose 0.1% and total nonresidential rose 0.6% in September. Construction costs rose 0.3%, so real construction spending fell 2.1%.
GS left its Q4 GDP tracking estimate unchanged at +1.8% q/q annualized and launched its past-quarter tracking estimate at +3.4%, unchanged on a rounded basis from the advance reading.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Above the 54.5 GS and median forecast, up from a prior 54.5. New orders and production rose while employment fell.
Down 2.7pt after a large September increase, still elevated.
Up 0.1pt, indicating slower deliveries for a larger share of respondents.
Revised down from the 56.0 flash and prior, below the 56.0 median forecast.
Well below the GS +0.2% and median +0.3% forecasts, driven by private residential improvements.
GS calculation: nominal spending less a 0.3% rise in construction costs.
Unchanged on a rounded basis from the advance reading.

risk_factors: Respondents cite inflationary pressure, volatile commodity markets and material shortages.
Production-material lead times are at 87 days, well above the 2019 average of 67 days.
Private residential improvements spending is volatile, with a 6% average monthly move over the past six months.
